about.title: Personal Injury Help in Pleasant Hill, California
about.longDescription: Pleasant Hill sits at a crossroads of daily commuter traffic, with Contra Costa Boulevard, I-680, Taylor Boulevard, and Monument Boulevard carrying much of the city's back-and-forth movement. Public records show 144 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, with 194 people hurt and 2 lives lost — numbers that reflect how often ordinary trips through town end in something no one planned for. Many of these reported crashes cluster on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., a stretch when work traffic and weekend plans tend to overlap. If you or someone you love has been hurt in one of these incidents, or in a fall, workplace accident, or other injury event in Pleasant Hill, LawProactive can help. We are a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney in the area. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money on your behalf. Reaching out costs nothing and puts you under no obligation.

whyChoose.title: What You Should Know Under California Law

items.title: A Filing Deadline Applies
items.desc: California generally gives you 2 years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, though claims against a government entity may require action within as little as 6 months. Waiting too long can close the door on your options.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation — reduced by your share of fault, but not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In an ordinary injury case, California places no limit on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. This can matter significantly for injuries that affect daily life long after the incident.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys connected through LawProactive work on contingency. That means legal help is available without upfront cost, and payment only comes from money recovered on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Pleasant Hill?
items.answer: California generally allows 2 years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government agency is involved, that window can shrink to as little as 6 months, so it's worth acting sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my accident?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means partial fault doesn't automatically bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do injury crashes tend to cluster in Pleasant Hill?
items.answer: Public crash records point to Contra Costa Boulevard, I-680, Taylor Boulevard, and Monument Boulevard as the corridors with the highest recorded collision counts, with Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showing more reported crashes than other times. These are neutral public-record counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning fees only apply if they recover money for you. There's no cost or obligation to find out where you stand.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is not a law firm. We're a free service that connects injured people in Pleasant Hill and throughout Contra Costa County with independent personal injury attorneys who can evaluate their situation.
